slides.title: Manipulator rigid-body dynamics
slides.text:
The Control problem for manipulators
•  Manipulator dynamics contain:
   –  inertia coupling
   –  Coriolis effects, centrifugal effects
   – gravity loading, friction
•  The equations become complicated for
   multi-joint robots.
•  General rigid-body dynamics:
              𝜏= 𝑀Θ ሷΘ + 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ + 𝐺Θ
•  where:
• 𝑀Θ →inertia matrix ; 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ  →Coriolis + centrifugal
• 𝐺Θ →gravity vector  ; 𝜏→ joint torque vector

                                                                                                           3

visualInspection.notes: M(q) qddot + V(q,qdot)+G(q); inertia coupling, Coriolis/centrifugal, gravity, friction mentioned. Diagram two links l1,m1 and l2,m2, downward m1g,m2g,g, torque arrows tau1,tau2; theta2 marked relative dashed local horizontal, not infer complete DH convention. Footer 3.

slides.title: Partitioned computed torque and friction
slides.text:
The Control problem for manipulators

•  Including friction effects:
          𝜏= 𝑀Θ ሷΘ + 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ + 𝐺Θ + 𝐹Θ, ሶΘ
   – where:
     𝐹Θ, ሶΘ  →friction/non-rigid-body effects
•  The problem of controlling such a complicated system can be handled by
   the partitioned controller:
                𝜏= 𝛼𝜏′ + 𝛽
•  Choose: 𝛼= 𝑀Θ
      𝛽= 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ + 𝐺Θ + 𝐹Θ, ሶΘ

slides.title: Practical ideal-model assumptions
slides.text:
Practical Considerations
•  The ideal nonlinear control laws assume:
   – continuous-time computation
   – exact model knowledge
   – no delay in sensing or actuation
•   In practice, these assumptions are not true.
•  Two major problems:
•  Computation time
   – model-based control needs many calculations
•  Model inaccuracy
   – real robots never match the model perfectly
   – parameters change with load, wear, friction, uncertainty


                                                                                                             6

visualInspection.notes: Continuous-time exact model zero sensing/actuation delay assumptions; compute cost and inaccurate load/wear/friction parameters. Footer 6.

slides.title: Sampling and digital implementation
slides.text:
Practical Considerations
Sampling and Digital Implementation:
•   Real manipulators are controlled by digital computers; Control is not truly continuous
•   Therefore, control is performed at a sampling rate
•   Sensors are read at discrete instants and Commands are updated at discrete instants
•  Sampling introduces:
    –  Delay; Approximation; Performance degradation
•    If sampling is slow:
    –  control quality drops
    –  tracking becomes poor
    –  stability can be affected
•    If sampling is fast:
    –  continuous-time assumption becomes more reasonable


                                                                                                           7

visualInspection.notes: Sensors/commands at discrete instants, delay/approximation/performance loss, slow sampling can affect stability; fast sampling only makes continuous approximation more reasonable. No numeric sampling threshold. Footer 7.

slides.title: Feedforward nonlinear control diagrams
slides.text:
Feedforward Nonlinear Control





          Model Based Manipulator Control System                              Feedforward Control Scheme
•  One way to improve practical implementation is to place
   the dynamic model outside the servo loop
•  The model produces feedforward torque
•  The servo loop adds correction using error feedback
      𝜏= model based torque + 𝐾𝑝𝐸+ 𝐾𝑣ሶ𝐸


                                                                                                           8

visualInspection.notes: Left exact-model loop uses sensed q,qdot in M,V,G,F; right model inputs are desired acceleration/velocity/position and directly adds torque-domain Kp E+Kv Edot. Output theta has prime-like mark on diagram, velocity theta dot. Feedback retained, model outside fast servo. Footer 8. Desired-state feedforward generally leaves model trajectory mismatch residual, requiring qualification of next-page homogeneous equation.

slides.title: Feedforward error equation and configuration dependence
slides.text:
Feedforward Nonlinear Control
•  From the feedforward scheme, the closed-loop error becomes:
                 ሷ𝐸+ 𝑀−1 Θ 𝐾𝑣ሶ𝐸+ 𝑀−1 Θ 𝐾𝑝𝐸= 0
•  Achieves:
   –  fast servo loop
   – model computations can be done separately
   – model-based torque can even be precomputed offline
   – useful when the trajectory is known in advance
•  Important observations:
-   This is not completely decoupled
-  Matrices 𝑀−1 𝜃 make the poles depend on configuration
-  So the effective dynamics change as the arm moves

                                                                                                           9

visualInspection.notes: Printed Eddot+M(q)^−1 Kv Edot+M(q)^−1 Kp E=0. Faster separate/offline model for known trajectory; not completely decoupled; poles depend on configuration. Scope poles as frozen-configuration and homogeneous equation as additional cancellation/constant-model assumption, not exact desired-state feedforward generally. Footer 9.

slides.title: Dual-rate computation split
slides.text:
Dual-rate computed-torque implementation

• Main idea:
•  The model-based control computations are expensive.
•  Computing full manipulator dynamics at every servo cycle may be difficult.
•  Solution:
   – run model computations at a slower rate
          • nonlinear dynamic model computation
          • background process
   – run servo feedback loop at a faster rate
          • servo feedback
          • error correction



                                                                                                          10

visualInspection.notes: Slow nonlinear dynamic model background process, fast servo/error feedback. No fixed frequency/ratio specified. Footer 10.

slides.title: Disturbance error coupling and equilibrium
slides.text:
Lack of Knowledge of Parameters

Effect of External Disturbances:
•  Examples: payload variation, external
    forces, friction changes, vibration,
   unmodeled dynamics
•   Disturbance torque:
    –  Let:       𝜏𝑑
    – be the disturbance torque vector.
    – Then the error dynamics become:
          ሷ𝐸+ 𝐾𝑣ሶ𝐸+ 𝐾𝑝𝐸= 𝑀−1 Θ 𝜏𝑑
    –  disturbances directly excite tracking error
    –  Steady-State Error : 𝐸= 𝐾𝑝−1𝑀−1 Θ 𝜏𝑑
Because 𝑀Θ is not diagonal, disturbance at one joint affects other joints

                                                                                                           12

visualInspection.notes: Diagram subtracts tau_d at arm input. Therefore positive M^-1 tau_d on E dynamics is consistent E=desired-actual. SSE Kp^-1 M^-1 tau_d assumes constant disturbance, equilibrium, invertibility. Non-diagonal inertia permits cross-joint effects; not necessarily every joint every configuration. Footer 12.

slides.title: Estimated versus actual dynamic model
slides.text:
Lack of Knowledge of Parameters
•  Model Uncertainty:
    –  Perfect knowledge of manipulator mean:
                        ෡𝑀Θ = 𝑀Θ
                              ෠𝑉Θ, ሶΘ = 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ
               Our Model                              Perfect Model                            ෠𝐺Θ = 𝐺Θ
                              ෠𝐹Θ, ሶΘ = 𝐹Θ, ሶΘ
•   Actual manipulator dynamics,
        𝜏= 𝑀Θ ሷΘ + 𝑉Θ ሶΘ + 𝐺Θ + 𝐹Θ ሶΘ
•   Controller uses estimated model:
          𝛼= ෡𝑀Θ   ; 𝛽= ෠𝑉+ ෠𝐺+ ෠𝐹
•   Closed Loop Equation:
ሷ𝐸+ 𝐾𝑣ሶ𝐸+ 𝐾𝑝𝐸= ෡𝑀−1 𝑀−෡𝑀 ሷΘ + 𝑉−෠𝑉+ 𝐺−෠𝐺+ 𝐹−෠𝐹
•   Perfect Decoupling will not be achieved.

                                                                                                          13

visualInspection.notes: Hat M,V,G,F versus true values; controller alpha=hatM,beta=hatV+hatG+hatF. Exact displayed residual hatM^-1[(M-hatM)qddot+(V-hatV)+(G-hatG)+(F-hatF)] is algebraically consistent; contains actual acceleration, not desired. Perfect-model residual zero; generic mismatch loses decoupling, not universal failure. Footer 13.

slides.title: Industrial joint-control rationale
slides.text:
Current Industrial-Robot control systems

•   In practice, many industrial robots do not use full
   nonlinear model-based control. Why?
   – model computation is expensive
   – parameter knowledge is incomplete
   – simpler control laws are often good enough
•  Most industrial robots use simple, robust control
   architectures.
•  No full decoupling is done.                             An Industrial                                                                          Robot
•  Each joint is often treated almost independently.
•  Controller gains are chosen to give acceptable
   performance over the workspace.


                                                                                                          14

visualInspection.notes: Source claims many/most industrial arms use simple robust almost independent joints, compute/model knowledge/good-enough cost-benefit. Photo illustrative no model-dependent engineering data. Treat prevalence as course statement, not current market survey. Footer 14.

Current Industrial-Robot control systems
Individual-Joint PID Control:
•   Control law:                                           •  𝐾𝑣, 𝐾𝑝, 𝐾𝑖 are diagonal gain matrices
•   Simplest industrial robot control is written as:     •  No model-based compensation is
          𝛼= 𝐼, 𝛽= 0                      used.
•  So the servo law becomes:                           •  Each joint is controlled as a separate
                                                    system.             𝜏′ = ሷΘ𝑑+ 𝐾𝑣ሶ𝐸+ 𝐾𝑝𝐸+ 𝐾𝑖න𝐸𝑑𝑡
                                                              •  This is essentially a PID-type joint
• 𝐸= Θ𝑑−Θ ; Often ሷΘ𝑑= 0 as it is unavailable.     controller.

slides.title: Joint-control limits and gravity compensation
slides.text:
Current Industrial-Robot control systems
•  Performance of Simple Joint Control:
    – Because there is no decoupling:
           • one joint motion affects the others
           • disturbance rejection is not perfect
    –  Fixed gains cannot give ideal critical damping for every robot posture.
    – Hence, “Average” gains are chosen.
•  Gravity compensation:
    –  To reduce static positioning error, gravity can be added to the control law:
                                𝜏′ = ሷΘ𝑑+ 𝐾𝑣ሶ𝐸+ 𝐾𝑝𝐸+ 𝐾𝑖න𝐸𝑑𝑡+ ෠𝐺Θ

    –  Gravity creates steady-state error.
    – Adding ෠𝐺Θ improves holding accuracy.
    –  This is a common industrial improvement over pure PID.

                                                                                                           16

visualInspection.notes: No exact decoupling; interactions and imperfect disturbance rejection, posture-varying damping so average gains. Adds hatG to PID/desired acceleration law. Gravity creates SSE blanket claim requires qualification: ideal stable unsaturated integral action can supply constant gravity with zero final E; PD has finite E. Same acceleration-to-torque unit omission as741. Footer 16.

slides.title: Lyapunov motivation and performance distinction
slides.text:
Lyapunov Stability Analysis
Main idea:
• We need a method that can prove stability without solving the differential
   equation.
•  Lyapunov’s method does this using an energy-like function.
•    If a positive function 𝑣𝑥 keeps decreasing along system trajectories, the system
    is stable.

Important Note:
•   Stability is not the same as performance.
•  A system may be stable but still respond slowly or poorly.
•  Lyapunov analysis tells us whether the system will settle,
   not how fast in every detail.

                                                                                                           17

visualInspection.notes: Energy-like positive function decreases along trajectories; stability without solving ODE. Stable not necessarily fast/good tracking. Wording will settle is too broad for mere Lyapunov stability; need asymptotic/invariance argument. Footer 17.

slides.title: Linear mass-spring-damper energy
slides.text:
Lyapunov Stability Analysis
Mass–Spring–Damper Stability by Energy Analysis:
•  System equation:     𝑚ሷ𝑥+ 𝑏ሶ𝑥+ 𝑘𝑥= 0

                               1        1
•   Total energy:      𝑣=  𝑚ሶ𝑥2 +  𝑘𝑥2
                               2        2                                                        To find Rest position
•  where:  first term = kinetic energy                                                  From steady-state analysis:
          second term = potential energy            𝑘𝑥= 0 is rest position
                                                ∴ 𝑥= 0•  Then,       ሶ𝑣= 𝑚ሶ𝑥ሷ𝑥+ 𝑘𝑥ሶ𝑥
•   Substitute the system equation: 𝑚ሷ𝑥= −𝑏ሶ𝑥−𝑘𝑥
•   So,         ሶ𝑣= −𝑏ሶ𝑥2
•   Since 𝑏> 0,  ሶ𝑣≤0
•  Energy keeps decreasing.
•  The system eventually comes to rest.


                                                                                                          18

visualInspection.notes: m xddot+b xdot+kx=0; v=1/2 m xdot²+1/2 kx²; derivative m xdot xddot+kx xdot=−b xdot²≤0. Rest kx=0 implies x=0 if k≠0. Require m,k>0 for positive definite energy and b>0 for dissipation. Derivative semidefinite in (x,xdot); asymptotic conclusion needs only invariant zero-derivative point, or positive-coefficient characteristic roots. Footer 18.

slides.title: Direct method conditions and domain
slides.text:
Lyapunov Stability Analysis
•   Previous analysis is a simple example of a more general technique called Lyapunov
    Stability Analysis or Lyapunov’s Second (or Direct Method).
•  General nonlinear system:      ሶ𝑋= 𝑓𝑋
•  where: 𝑋 is the state vector ; 𝑓𝑋 may be nonlinear
•  Lyapunov function 𝑣𝑋 must satisfy:
    – 𝑣𝑋  is continuous and has continuous first partial derivatives
      and 𝑣𝑋> 0 ∀ 𝑥 𝑒𝑥𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑡 𝑣0 = 0
    – Along trajectories:  ሶ𝑣𝑋≤0
•    If:  ሶ𝑣𝑋< 0  then, asymptotic stability

Intuition:
• 𝑣𝑋  acts like stored energy.
•   If it always decreases, the state cannot grow without bound.
•  The state is pulled toward equilibrium.


                                                                                                          19

visualInspection.notes: Xdot=f(X), C1 positive-definite v with v(0)=0; vdot≤0 stability and <0 away from equilibrium asymptotic stability. Omitted equilibrium/regularity/local-domain qualification and compact-sublevel/properness for global boundedness. Cannot infer globally bounded state from arbitrary positive decreasing function alone. Footer 19.

   – 𝑥𝑘𝑥> 0 for 𝑥≠0
•  Construct Lyapunov function:
                                         𝑥                         1
                 𝑣𝑥, ሶ𝑥=   ሶ𝑥2 + න 𝑘𝜆𝑑𝜆
                         2                                         0

Sign conditions xdot*b(xdot)>0 and x*k(x)>0 away0. Candidate v=.5 xdot²+integral0^x k(lambda)dlambda; negative x integral remains positive. sourceIssues.finding: Desired-state model diagram734 does not generally yield the homogeneous actual-M equation735 away from tracking; moving-system poles are also a frozen-configuration description.
sourceIssues.handling: Explicitly derive residual and state zero-residual/frozen-configuration assumptions for simplified calculations.

sourceIssues.finding: α=I and unscaled desired acceleration are added to physical torque-domain PID terms; no normalization/inertia scale is stated.
sourceIssues.handling: Use desired acceleration zero in SI examples; explicitly test the missing scale rather than silently treat acceleration as torque.

sourceIssues.finding: Gravity creates steady-state error is overbroad for the displayed ideal PID architecture.
sourceIssues.handling: Distinguish PD residual error from PID integral-state load balance, with stability and actuator-limit assumptions stated.

sourceIssues.finding: The linear example lists only b>0 explicitly and jumps from vdot≤0 to rest.
sourceIssues.handling: State m,k>0 for positive definiteness; use the zero-derivative invariant-set argument, not strict negativity in the full state.

sourceIssues.finding: Informal direct-method statements omit equilibrium/domain/regularity and global boundedness conditions, and negative derivative must exclude the equilibrium.
sourceIssues.handling: Make local assumptions explicit, distinguish nonpositive from strictly negative derivative and qualify global claims by compact sublevels/properness.

sourceIssues.finding: Informal settling language can conflate Lyapunov stability with asymptotic convergence.
sourceIssues.handling: Separate remaining-near equilibrium, convergence and transient-rate properties in the question scope.

sourceIssues.finding: The right-hand prose applies zero velocity to all trajectories and writes −kx despite the nonlinear k(x) example. The ODE xddot=−kx itself has nonzero solutions.
sourceIssues.handling: Interpret only trajectories remaining in zero dissipation; persistent zero velocity implies zero acceleration, then nonlinear k(x)=0 forces x=0 under the strict sign condition.
